strengths: Novel application of Multi-Armed Bandit framework to context chunk selection, providing an intuitive exploration-exploitation approach that naturally extends beyond static similarity-based methods

Comprehensive experimental analysis including effective ablation studies (Table 3) isolating the contribution of MAB vs. alternatives, progressive quality analysis (Figures 3-4) showing consistent improvement, and hyperparameter sensitivity investigation
Well-motivated probe-based initialization strategy that leverages LLM's reasoning trace generation to address UCB cold-start problem, improving early-stage chunk selection efficiency

Clear presentation with effective figures and comprehensive implementation details enabling reproducibility, with commitment to release code and data

Sound technical execution of the methodology with correct UCB implementation and probe-based initialization

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily applies standard UCB algorithm (Auer et al., 2002) to chunk selection without novel algorithmic insights or theoretical analysis

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (LongBench, InfiniteBench) with diverse models and scales, including out-of-domain generalization tests and extension to longer contexts (16k-128k tokens)

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines standard techniques (UCB algorithm from Auer et al. 2002, established DPO, existing chunk-based sampling) without substantial algorithmic innovation; main contribution is pragmatic combination rather than conceptual advance
